Description: In situ voting experiment run beside the first round of the 2017 French presidential election (Saturday 22 April 2017 in Martinique) at the Ecole Dillon D in Fort-de-France, which housed polling stations 17, 18 and 19: voters were invited after their official vote into a separate room and each filled one sheet with two experimental ballots, instant-runoff and Borda-4, over the 11 official candidates (524 took part, 508 usable sheets). This table: the instant-runoff ballots (write 1 to 11 against the candidates; all 11 were requested, at least one required). 480 ballots, 5,137 rows; 461 rank all 11 and 19 rank 1 to 9. One row per ballot x ranked candidate; item = candidate code c01..c11 in the source's candidate numbering (candidate k of the PrefLib file, which is the order printed on the ballot; names not stored); resp = position, 1 = first. id = the ballot 1..n, expanded from PrefLib's weighted profile in its line order (the order of casting is not in the source); the same participants' Borda-4 ballots are kamwa_2017_fortdefrance_borda4, but ids do not link the two tables. The paper counts 505 valid IRV ballots; PrefLib holds 480. Self-selected participants (524 of the 2,217 who voted at the three stations), not a sample of French voters. Rankings layout (data/rankings/README.md).
Reference: Kamwa, E., Joseph, G. & Roger, A. (2020). Une expérimentation de deux modes de scrutin en Martinique lors du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle de 2017. Revue d'économie politique, 130(5), 759-798. https://doi.org/10.3917/redp.305.0081. Data distributed by PrefLib as dataset 00072 (french-experiments-rankings), https://www.preflib.org/dataset/00072.
Notes: Script data/rankings/kamwa_2017_fortdefrance.py; design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Read from PrefLib-Data commit 03f5a88 file 00072-00000002.soi (sha256 pinned), a weighted profile expanded to one id per ballot. PrefLib holds 480 of the 505 valid IRV ballots in the paper (Table 4): every candidate's first-place count is at or below the paper's, and the 19 incomplete rankings match the paper's 505 - 486 complete, so the 25 absent ballots would be complete rankings; which and why is not in the source. No covariates: the sheet's questionnaire is not in PrefLib. Licence: no licence is stated by PrefLib.
